newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 25.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Sources close to talks between Westpac Banking Corp and the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission believe the ACCC has approved in principle, and under special conditions, the proposed A$1.4 billion takeover by Westpac of the Bank of Melbourne. Pge 1.

An ICI Australia spokesman said yesterday the company is unlikely to provide extra financial information to shareholders about the proposed sale of its drug division to Zeneca, despite the sale having an impact on the future of ICIA's future earnings. The spokesman said ICIA believed it had already provided enough information and expected a fair value for the sale of the division. Page 21.

Broking houses Merrill Lynch and HSBC James Capel were heavily involved in the trading of a 1.5 per cent stake in John Fairfax Holdings Ltd yesterday, which is believed to have gone to New Zealand's Brierley Investments Ltd. The move would see BIL move closer to its goal of a 25 per cent stake in Fairfax. Page 21.

Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation confirmed yesterday it would join Tele-Communications Inc to pay A$850 million for a 40 per cent stake in Cablevision's sports TV business in the United States. The purchase will give NewsCorp a share in New York's Madison Square Gardens, as well as seven regional networks called SportsChannel, and see it competing directly with US cable sports giant ESPN. Page 22.

Telstra chief executive Frank Blount said the Federal Government had instructed the national carrier to be ready for floating by October, which would see it listed on schedule in November. The Federal Government is expecting to reap A$8 billion from the float, but some market analysts expect the amount to be as high as A$10 billion. Page 23.

Super League chief executive John Ribot resigned yesterday to take up the position of sole owner of the Melbourne Super League franchise. His departure is expected to move the possible compromise between Super League and the Australian Rugby League a step closer, which would in turn be a step towards stemming losses in Australia's pay-TV industry. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

AAPT chief executive Larry Williams said yesterday the telecommunications carrier-in-waiting, which is hoping to be granted a carrier licence by the Federal Government next month, is considering a share market listing in an attempt to raise funds for cable infrastructure and acquisitions. Page 19.

After suffering a defeat in the Federal Court yesterday, it is expected ICI Australia will make out-of-court payments of up to A$100 million to cattle producers whose stock was contaminated by ICI's Helix pesticide. However, ICI said it would appeal the decision on the grounds it met the requirements of regulators as well as industry standards at the time of registering Helix. Page 19.

Southern Pacific Petroleum and Central Pacific Minerals, known as the Rundle twins, yesterday announced that after 20 years the Stuart oil shale deposit in Queensland is finally moving ahead with the completion of a A$90 million capital raising that clears the final hurdle in the project's development. Page 20.

Telecasters North Queensland secretary Barry Sechos said the proposed restructuring plans - including a proposed reduction in capital to 18.2 million shares, matching its holding in Ten Network stock - that are to be voted on by shareholders at the end of this month would not go ahead until the ownership debate of Ten is resolved. Page 21.

Rio Tinto's Canadian joint venture partner, Aber Resources, has told the Vancouver Stock Exchange that grades of as much as 6.2 carats per tonne have been found in the second diamond-bearing pipe of the Diavik diamond discovery in Canada's remote Northwest Territories. Page 21.

American Express regional vice-president John Schaap told an Institute of Bankers lunch yesterday that Amex may move towards issuing its plastic cards through the banking system. Schaap said Amex wanted to get optimum use out of the world's most recognisble card in an era of increasing consolidation in global financial services. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Speaking at an American Chamber of Commerce lunch in Sydney yesterday, Telstra chief executive Frank Blount said the telecommunications carrier had been given orders by the Federal Government to be ready for a listing this year. Blount said Telstra was negotiating its position in a global telecommunications alliance in preparation for the float. Page 29.

A four-man committee of Australian National Industries is considering a report by Bob Ellicott, QC, into the controversial purchase by Kerry Packer's Consolidated Press Holdings of German waste-to-energy business ABT, and may look at taking legal action aainst CPH if the report, and the board, believe action would be commercially justifiable. Page 29.

Australia's All Ordinaries index demonstrated its resilience yesterday, after shrugging off the biggest points fall on Wall St since the 1987 stockmarket crash. While the Dow Jones index crashed by 192.25 points to close at 7,604.26 on Monday, the All Ords did initially fall by 33.8 points, but recovered to close down 17.9 points at 2688.4. Page 29.

There has been some resistance to the planned float by Boral of its natural gas distribution business Envestra, and Boral has been forced to reprice the planned A$850 million float to win institutional support. Annual income yields on Envestra have been lifted from 7.2 per cent to 7.75 per cent for the 1998 financial year. Page 31.

The Financial Sector Union claims the ANZ bank is concerned only with cutting jobs and nothing else following a meeting between the bank and the union over the cutting of 190 jobs in New South Wales over the next three months. The union said the bank is being ruthless, and union concerns are falling on deaf ears. Page 31.

Despite interest by RG Capital in taking up the last unused UHF television frequency for a concept called "city TV" that would serve the local city rather than offering nationally networked programs, the Federal Government is unlikely to embrace the idea of a fourth commercial service. Page 31.
THE AGE

Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto sent financial markets into a spin yesterday when he appeared to suggest a major rift with the United States on exchange rate policy. While Wall St's Dow Jones index fell to its lowest level since the 1987 stockmrket crash, Australia's All Ordinaries index, like that of other Asia Pacific markets, appeared less concerned, dropping early but regaining to be 17.9 points down at 2688.4. Page B1.

Telstra chief executive Frank Blount said yesterday that unless market conditions get in the way, the float of the national telecommunications carrier should take place in November. The Federal Government is preparing a prospectus for the one-third float of Telstra, which should glean between A$8 billion and A$12 billion. Page B1.

Hawker Richardson shares climbed 8.4 per cent, or 14 cents, yesterday, as investors backed Austrim's offer of A$1.60 a share for the diverse manufacturer. As directors of Hawker Richardson met last night to consider the offer, analysts predicted the bid ould be rejected as insufficient, as shares closed yesterday at A$1.80. Page B3.

In a wide-ranging review commissioned by Federal Science and Technology Minister Peter McGauran, the Federal Government's chief scientific adviser Professor John Stocker called on the Government to spell out a vision for Australia's industrial development and reinstate funding for research and development by both universities and business. Page B3.

Shares in John Fairfax Holdings Ltd shifted yesterday when stockbroker HSBC James Capel, believed to be acting for New Zealand-based Brierley Investments, bought 8.62 million shares at between A$3.20 and A$3.21 each from Merrill Lynch, which sold 8.73 milion. Page B3.

In a meeting on Monday night, shareholders in fruit distribution and exporting group Geoffrey Thompson Holdings approved the appointment of two new directors, the re-election of six directors, and the re-election of 80-year-old chairman Geoffrey William Tompson senior. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
